site: Worthington Community Center, 345 E Wilson Bridge Rd
about: The Holiday Party is listed in the Special Events section of the City of Worthington's Parks and Recreation pages, alongside the department's other community events.
The city's own description calls it a night of fun and festive activities, and it says the party is completely free.
Santa and his reindeer visit the Worthington Community Center for the evening, and the city lists carnival games and seasonal cheer as part of the night.
The Worthington Community Center is at 345 E Wilson Bridge Rd, Worthington, OH 43085, and its main phone number is (614) 436-2743.
The center also has an indoor aquatics facility with two pools, so it is a building many Worthington families already know.
The party runs two hours, from 6 to 8 PM on a Friday, which suits families who want a school night free evening out.
The city's holiday page is tagged with Christmas and Santa, and a Columbus area Santa guide published for 2026 lists the party among central Ohio visits with Santa.
For sports and facility questions the city lists a separate sports line at (614) 786-7366, while party questions go to the main center number.
faq: When is the Worthington Holiday Party?
Friday, December 11, 2026, from 6 to 8 PM.
Where is it held?
At the Worthington Community Center, 345 E Wilson Bridge Rd, Worthington, OH 43085.
Is it free?
Yes. The City of Worthington lists the party as completely free.
Who is attending?
Santa and his reindeer visit during the party.
What activities are planned?
Carnival games and festive activities for families.
Who hosts the event?
The City of Worthington Parks and Recreation department.
Who can I call with questions?
The Worthington Community Center at (614) 436-2743.

kids: Make a craft and play period games
Receive a gift from a very famous visitor
about: The Worthington Historical Society describes Children's Christmas as a popular holiday tradition, and it is open to children in grades 3 to 5.
Three Saturday sessions are offered, December 5, 12 and 19, each from 4 to 8 PM, and a family signs up for one of them.
Children prepare and eat a typical early 1800s meal, then hear Christmas stories from the period.
The evening also includes a house tour, period games, a craft, traditional songs and a look at school traditions of the time.
Every child receives a gift from a very famous visitor, a surprise the society keeps under wraps on its event page.
Advance registration is required. Tickets went on sale online on November 1 and cost $35 per child.
Questions go to Children's Christmas Committee Chair Dianne Hoover at 614-888-2326, and volunteers can reach the society at 614-885-1247.
Because every child attends just one of the three Saturdays, the program stays small enough for each guest to join the meal and the games.
Families who also want to browse the society's Shop and Doll Museum at the Old Rectory should note that both close for the winter beginning December 20.
faq: When are the Children's Christmas sessions?
Saturdays, December 5, 12 and 19, 2026, from 4 to 8 PM. Families pick one date.
Which children can attend?
Children in grades 3 to 5.
What does a ticket cost?
$35 per child.
Is registration needed?
Yes. Advance registration is required through the society's online booking.
What will children do?
Eat an early 1800s style meal, hear Christmas stories, tour the house, play period games, make a craft and sing traditional songs.
Who is the visitor with the gift?
The society calls the visitor very famous and keeps the name a surprise.
Who answers questions?
Committee chair Dianne Hoover at 614-888-2326.

kids: Listen to ghost stories of the season
about: On Thursday, December 10, a historic house in Old Worthington opens for an evening tour, with the first group starting at 6:30 PM.
The house is decorated and aglow for Christmas, and history interpreters share how the town's founders celebrated in 1803.
Their stories run through the 1800s and early 1900s, from Christmas stockings and trees to ghost stories and gift giving.
Reservations are required. Tickets cost $15, are bought online and are non-refundable.
The society cautions that the house has several flights of stairs and that guests should be able to navigate steps and stand during portions of the tour.
The evening is listed from 6:30 to 8 PM, a short outing that fits a school night. Online booking goes through the FareHarbor page the society links from its event listing.
The tour is a separate ticketed program from the society's Saturday Children's Christmas sessions for grades 3 to 5. Tickets are sold online only, at $15.00 each.

A week earlier, on Wednesday, December 2, Old Worthington holds Illuminated Shopping from 6 to 9 PM, with live holiday music, luminaries lining High Street, a horse drawn carriage and local retailers open late.
faq: When is the Christmas Traditions tour?
Thursday, December 10, 2026, with tours starting at 6:30 PM.
What does a ticket cost?
$15 each, sold online and non-refundable.
Are reservations required?
Yes.
What will we hear about?
Christmas in Worthington from 1803 through the early 1900s, including stockings, trees, ghost stories and gift giving.
Can I get a refund?
No. The society states that tickets are non-refundable.
Are there stairs?
Yes. The society notes several flights of stairs and asks guests to be able to navigate steps and stand during portions of the tour.
How long is the evening?
The listing runs from 6:30 to 8 PM.
How do I reserve a spot?
Book online through the society's FareHarbor booking page linked from the event listing.

kids: Build a wooden toy with the elves
Paint the toy and take it home
Get a photo with Santa and Mrs. Claus
site: Westerville Community Center, 350 N Cleveland Ave
Nov 30 to Dec 6, morning and evening sessions
about: Snowflake Castle is a Westerville Parks and Recreation winter event where children build a toy in Santa's Workshop with the elves.
The 2026 event has a new home, the Westerville Community Center at 350 N Cleveland Ave, because Everal Barn is closed for renovations through winter 2027.

The multipurpose rooms at the south end of the building hold the event, and free parking is at the south end of the community center lot, reached from the Cleveland Ave entrance across from the Westerville Sports Complex.

Each ticket covers a wooden toy to paint and take home plus a photo with Santa and Mrs. Claus. Guests can also join a storybook trail, see Santa's sleigh and the trains, and enjoy coloring and holiday movies while they wait.
Tickets are $15 per child, sold online only, and adults who accompany a ticketed child do not need a ticket, with up to two adults per child and a limit of six tickets per household.
Sessions run Monday through Friday from 9 to 11:30 AM and 5 to 7:30 PM, on Saturday, December 5 from 9 to 11:30 AM and 4 to 7 PM, and on Sunday, December 6 from 10:30 AM to 12:30 PM and 2 to 4:30 PM.
The city suggests ages 10 and under, notes that the event sells out, and offers no waitlist, and tickets are non-transferable.

A sensory friendly Snowflake Castle takes place on Sunday, November 29 from 1 to 4 PM with separate registration, and there is no Snowflake Castle on Monday, December 7, when a Paws and Claus event runs from 6 to 8 PM.

A holiday craft area in Multipurpose 5 needs no ticket, and proceeds from the Westerville Senior Craftique items go to the Westerville Senior Association. Questions go to santa@westerville.org or (614) 901-6560.
faq: When is Snowflake Castle 2026?
Monday, November 30 through Sunday, December 6, 2026, in morning and afternoon or evening sessions.
Where is Snowflake Castle this year?
At the Westerville Community Center, 350 N Cleveland Ave, Westerville, OH 43082, in the multipurpose rooms at the south end.
How much are tickets?
$15 per child, including a toy and a photo with Santa. Tickets are online only.
Do adults need tickets?
No. Up to two adults may accompany each ticketed child.
What ages is it for?
The city suggests ages 10 and under.
Does it sell out?
Yes. The city says the event is very popular and does sell out, and it offers no waitlist.
Why is it not at Everal Barn?
Everal Barn is undergoing renovations through winter 2027.
